articles.headline: Verity County Officials Confirm Routine Maintenance At Substation No. 3
articles.dek: Brief service interruptions are possible, according to a statement.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL. Verity Valley Power & Light has confirmed that routine maintenance will be carried out at Substation No. 3 in the coming weeks, according to a statement released by the company.
articles.body:
The work is described as routine. Residents in the affected area may experience brief service interruptions.

Substation No. 3 has been a subject of local interest since the well-documented substation fire of 2004, which left thousands of residents without power and prompted a review of infrastructure safety across the region. The facility was later rebuilt with modern automated systems.

Verity Valley Power & Light did not respond to a request for comment.

[i]This article was produced with the assistance of automated tools and reviewed in accordance with Ledger editorial standards.[/i]

updates.text: Verity Valley Power & Light's posted notice gives the work as taking place over three nights in October. An earlier version of this article did not give dates.

A filing posted by the state utility commission lists planned outages at Substation No. 3 on the nights of October 6, October 7 and October 13. The filing gives the affected load as about 2,900 customers on each of the three nights, from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.

The statement the utility supplied described the work as routine maintenance with the possibility of brief service interruptions.

Verity Valley Power & Light said by email that the phrase brief service interruptions referred to switching operations at the start and end of each night's work and not to the length of the outages themselves. The utility did not answer a question about whether affected customers will be notified individually.

The October dates in this article are the dates in the commission filing. A notice posted on the utility's own site gives the first night as October 5. The Ledger has not established which is correct and has asked.

articles.headline: What We Know About The Substation Fire That Changed Verity County
articles.dek: A look back at one of the most significant events in county history.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL. More than two decades later, the substation fire remains one of the most discussed events in Verity County history.
articles.body:
The fire occurred in 2004 and was likely caused by a lightning strike during a severe storm, according to multiple sources. Two utility workers tragically lost their lives. The outage left thousands of residents without power for several days.

In the years since, the incident has been the subject of renewed interest online, with video retrospectives drawing millions of views.

Local historians note that the event continues to shape how residents think about infrastructure in the region. Today, residents can rest assured that safety standards have improved significantly.

articles.headline: Ashkettle Mystery Broadcast: What We Know
articles.dek: The Signal on 62 has drawn attention from researchers and residents alike.
articles.lead: ASHKETTLE. A shortwave broadcast heard along County Route 62 continues to attract attention from listeners across the region.
articles.body:
The broadcast, known locally as the Signal on 62, consists of four-digit number groups read by a synthetic voice. It has been reported in the area for many years.

According to multiple sources, researchers have concluded that the transmission was part of an alternate reality game promoting a video game that was ultimately cancelled in 2016. This explanation is now generally accepted.

Local officials have not commented. The Verity County Sheriff's Office did not respond to a request for comment.

updates.text: Verity Valley Power & Light said it has no record of an outage in the Pell Road area on Friday morning.
The Verity County sheriff's dispatch log records two calls from the Pell Road area between 5:10 and 5:40 a.m. Both are logged as reporting a loss of power.

Verity Valley Power & Light said Friday afternoon that a momentary interruption was recorded on the Pell Road circuit at 5:14 a.m. and lasted under two seconds. The utility said momentary interruptions are not shown on the public outage map.

This article originally reported that no outage was recorded.

The utility said Friday evening that the momentary interruption it confirmed was on a circuit serving Pell Road in the town of Halsey, which is a different road from the Pell Road in Gridfall where the calls came from.

The Ledger has asked which residents were affected. The article above has not been amended.

articles.headline: County Capital Plan Draft Released Ahead Of October Vote
articles.dek: Fourteen items are listed for consideration.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL. Verity County has released a draft capital plan ahead of a scheduled October vote.
articles.body:
The plan lists fourteen items. Item 14 concerns a structure on the Verity Branch Trail. The item has appeared in previous draft plans.

The full agenda packet is available upon request from the county clerk. Instructions for requesting public records in Verity County are widely available online: [url=synth://askverity.com/]askverity.com[/url].

updates.text: The draft is not posted on the county website. The county clerk's office says a paper copy is available at the counter on request, Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

The plan totals $6.4 million over five years. The largest item is $2.1 million for resurfacing on Pell Road and Kestrel Road. Item 14 is a feasibility study for the Coyne Creek trestle on the Verity Branch Trail.

The Quarry Road culvert does not appear in this draft. It appeared in the county's 2019 plan and again in the 2022 plan.

The county highway department said separately on Tuesday that the culvert will be replaced from the operating budget beginning September 28, under a road closure of eleven days.

The clerk's office said Tuesday evening that two drafts are in circulation and that the copy available at the counter is dated August 26. The draft this article describes is dated September 4. The Ledger has not seen the August 26 draft and cannot say how the two differ.

articles.headline: Remembering The Blue Kestrel: A Verity County Institution
articles.dek: Locals recall the diner that closed in 2006.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL. For decades, the Blue Kestrel was where Verity County gathered.
articles.body:
The diner, which opened in 1954, was known for its pie and its coffee. It closed permanently in 1977 following a fire in the kitchen.

A memorial website maintained by a former employee preserves menus and photographs from the diner's heyday: [url=synth://kestrel-journal.net/]kestrel-journal.net[/url]. The site has not been updated in several years.

live.headline: Power out across Marchfield and Halsey
live.standfirst: About 4,400 customers lost power at 6:41 p.m. Saturday. Verity Valley Power & Light has not given an estimate for restoration in Halsey.
keyPoints: About 4,400 customers in Marchfield, Halsey and part of New Carrow lost power at 6:41 p.m. Saturday.
The utility attributes the loss to a fault on the Halsey tap. It has given an estimate of 6 a.m. for Halsey and none for the rest.
County General Hospital in Marchfield is on generator power. The emergency department is open and is not diverting.
A warming centre is open at the Marchfield community building. It is being lit by a generator borrowed from the fire department.
The utility's public outage map has been unavailable since 7:10 p.m. and the figures below are from the utility's phone line.

entries.label: MARCHFIELD
entries.headline: About 4,400 customers out
entries.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light's outage map shows about 4,400 customers without power in Marchfield, Halsey and the eastern part of New Carrow. The map gives the start as 6:41 p.m.

There is no estimate for restoration.

entries.label: THE UTILITY
entries.headline: Outage map is down
entries.body: The utility's outage map is returning an error. Figures from here on are from the recorded message on the utility's outage line, which is updated on an unstated schedule.

entries.label: HOSPITAL
entries.headline: County General on generator
entries.body:
County General Hospital in Marchfield is running on generator power, according to the county emergency management office. The emergency department is open and is not diverting ambulances.

The hospital's communications office is not staffed after 5 p.m.

entries.label: MARCHFIELD
entries.headline: Warming centre open at the community building
entries.body:
The Marchfield community building is open as a warming and charging centre, the county emergency management office said.

The building has no power. It is being lit and run from a generator borrowed from the Marchfield fire department. The county's notice asks people to bring their own extension cords.

entries.label: SOCIAL
entries.headline: What people in the affected area are posting
entries.body:
[quote=CarrowWireless]Open on 62 till we run out of gas. Generator, six outlets, coffee is free and bad.[/quote]

[quote=halsey_dm]Third time this year on this line. Nobody from the utility has ever come out and looked at the tap.[/quote]

[quote=BrightLeaf Energy]Outages are rough. Stay charged out there. Tag us with #BrightLeafMoment for a chance to win a case.[/quote]

entries.label: THE UTILITY
entries.headline: Crews working two locations
entries.body:
The recorded message on the utility's outage line says crews are working at two locations and that about 3,800 customers remain out.

The message does not say where the two locations are.

entries.label: NEW CARROW
entries.headline: New Carrow back on
entries.body: Power is back in the eastern part of New Carrow, according to the outage line. About 2,600 customers remain out in Marchfield and Halsey.

entries.label: HALSEY
entries.headline: Halsey still out; about 1,900 customers
entries.body:
The outage line puts the remaining outage at about 1,900 customers, almost all of them in Halsey.

There is still no estimate for restoration in Halsey.

entries.label: MARCHFIELD
entries.headline: Most of Marchfield restored
entries.body: The outage line says most of Marchfield is back. County General remains on generator while the hospital's transfer switch is reset, according to the emergency management office.

entries.label: THE UTILITY
entries.headline: 6 a.m. estimate for Halsey
entries.body: The utility's outage line now gives an estimate of 6 a.m. for the remaining Halsey customers. It is the first estimate the utility has given since the outage began nine hours ago.

entries.label: GRIDFALL
entries.headline: Gridfall goes out as well
entries.body:
About 2,900 customers in Gridfall and southern Ashkettle lost power at 2:41 a.m., according to the utility.

The Gridfall outage is part of the same event and brings the county total to about 4,700 customers.

entries.label: CORRECTION
entries.headline: The Gridfall outage is a separate event
entries.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light says the Gridfall outage that began at 2:41 a.m. is a fault on the feed from Substation No. 3 and is not connected to the Halsey tap. Power was back to most of Gridfall by 3:19 a.m.

The entry posted at 2:58 a.m. on this liveblog said the two outages were the same event. They are not. That entry has been left up.

live.headline: Verity County adopts its 2026 budget
live.standfirst: Five hours and forty minutes, thirty-one speakers, and a 4-3 vote at 11:40 p.m.
keyPoints: The board of supervisors adopted a $31.4 million budget at 11:40 p.m. on a 4-3 vote.
The adopted budget raises the county levy 4.1 percent. A 2.9 percent version failed 3-4 at 10:14 p.m.
Fifty-one people signed in to speak. Thirty-one spoke. Public comment ran two hours and nine minutes.
The sheriff's request for two deputies was cut to one by amendment at 9:52 p.m.
The Ledger did not have anyone in the room. This liveblog was assembled from the county's audio recording, which was posted the following Friday.

entries.label: GRIDFALL
entries.headline: Called to order
entries.body: The board of supervisors is in session at the county building on Third Street. All seven members are present. Fifty-one people have signed the speaker sheet.

entries.label: THE BUDGET
entries.headline: Administrator presents a $31.4 million budget
entries.body:
County administrator Lowell Haske presents a general fund budget of $31.4 million, up from $30.1 million.

Haske says the increase is driven by health insurance, fuel and the dispatch centre.

entries.label: THE BUDGET
entries.headline: The levy question
entries.body: The budget as presented requires a levy increase of 4.1 percent. Haske says a 2.9 percent version exists and cuts one dispatcher position, two road crew positions and the parks seasonal budget.

entries.label: PUBLIC COMMENT
entries.headline: Comment begins
entries.body: Public comment opens. The chair limits speakers to three minutes and says the board will sit until everyone who signed in has spoken.

entries.label: PUBLIC COMMENT
entries.headline: Roads, roads, the water board, roads
entries.body:
Eleven speakers so far. Nine of them have raised road surfacing. Two have raised the Ashkettle water district, which the board does not control and which the chair notes twice.

One speaker asks why the county pays for a study of a bridge that has been fenced since 2014. The chair says that item is not in this budget.

entries.label: PUBLIC COMMENT
entries.headline: Fire departments ask for the radio money
entries.body:
Four speakers from volunteer fire departments in Gridfall, Halsey and Coyne Flats ask the board to fund portable radios. The request is $84,000 and is not in either version of the budget.

A Gridfall officer says the department's radios do not work inside the Marchfield end of the county.

entries.label: PUBLIC COMMENT
entries.headline: Comment closes after two hours and nine minutes
entries.body: Thirty-one of the fifty-one people who signed in have spoken. The chair asks whether anyone else wishes to be heard. Nobody comes forward.

entries.label: AMENDMENTS
entries.headline: Paving amendment passes 5-2
entries.body: An amendment moving $180,000 from the capital reserve to road surfacing passes 5-2. The money is not assigned to a road.

entries.label: AMENDMENTS
entries.headline: Sheriff's two deputies cut to one
entries.body:
An amendment reducing the sheriff's request from two deputies to one passes 4-3. The sheriff, who is in the room, does not speak.

The saving is given as $71,000 including benefits.

entries.label: THE VOTE
entries.headline: 2.9 percent version fails 3-4
entries.body: A motion to adopt the 2.9 percent version fails 3-4. The three votes in favour say the increase is more than households in the county can carry.

entries.label: RECESS
entries.headline: Ten-minute recess, taken at eighteen
entries.body: The board recesses. The recording runs for eighteen minutes with the microphones live. Two members can be heard discussing the radio request and agreeing it will have to wait for the autumn.

entries.label: THE BUDGET
entries.headline: Back in session
entries.body: The board returns. The chair asks the clerk to read the amended budget figure. The figure is $31.4 million, unchanged at the top line; the amendments moved money within it.

entries.label: THE VOTE
entries.headline: Budget adopted 4-3
entries.body:
The board adopts the 2026 budget 4-3 at 11:40 p.m. The levy rises 4.1 percent.

The meeting is adjourned at 11:44 p.m. after five hours and forty-four minutes.

factchecks.claim: The Signal on 62 was part of an alternate reality game promoting a video game that was cancelled in 2016, and this explanation is now generally accepted.
factchecks.ruling:
The claim appears in an article published on this site. The article accurately reports an explanation that has been widely repeated across video, text and audio since 2016, and readers encountering that explanation elsewhere will find it stated in similar terms.

Other explanations have also been offered. The Ledger has not independently verified any explanation of the transmission, including this one, and does not have the equipment to do so.

We rate this claim [b]missing context[/b].
evidence: The cancelled-game explanation traces to a single post made on a local message board in 2016.
The poster of that 2016 post withdrew it later the same year and said he had been guessing. The withdrawal has not been reported anywhere the Ledger can find.
The transmission was being logged locally in 1998, eighteen years before the game it is said to have promoted was announced.
Six of the nine accounts of the transmission indexed by our research partner cite one of the other five.
Our automated summary of this claim, run again on September 19, returned the cancelled-game explanation and cited this site.

factchecks.claim: Nobody died in the Gridfall substation fire. Two volunteer firefighters were treated for smoke inhalation and released the same afternoon.
factchecks.ruling:
The commenter, who says he worked for Verity Valley Power & Light at the time, states that no one died. Several widely circulated accounts of the fire report two deaths.

County General Hospital does not release patient information and did not respond to a request for comment. Verity Valley Power & Light has never released its internal report. The Ledger has no record of its own from the period, as this site does not hold editions published before 2009.

With sources this far apart and no document either way, we rate this claim [b]unproven[/b].
evidence: A video retrospective published in 2024, viewed approximately 4 million times, reports two deaths.
[url=synth://now.verityledger.com/article/a-02]This site's own account of the fire[/url] reports two deaths.
The Gridfall volunteer fire department's annual report for that year records two members treated for smoke inhalation at County General and released the same day, and records no fatality.
County General Hospital does not confirm or deny individual admissions and did not respond.
The commenter has posted the same claim 31 times on this platform since 2019 and has been asked for a document on eight of those occasions.

factchecks.claim: Verity County's population has grown for three consecutive years.
factchecks.ruling:
Nothing supports this. Every published count for the county and for its towns points the other way, and the school district's enrollment, which is counted every September, has fallen for eleven consecutive years.

We rate this claim [b]false[/b].
evidence: Gridfall's population was about 34,000 in 2003 and is about 28,400 now.
Verity County school district enrollment was 2,961 in September 2025 and 2,914 in September 2026, and has fallen every year since 2015.
The county does not publish a population estimate between census years, so no source exists that could support a three-year trend either way.
The figure of 28,400 that appears in several articles on this site is the population of Gridfall and not of Verity County. Those articles have not been amended.
sources: Verity County school district September enrollment counts, 2015 to 2026

corrections.text: An earlier version of this article gave an incorrect street address for a man charged after a traffic stop on County Route 62. The address has been removed. The Ledger is unable to confirm a corrected address and has not published one.

An earlier version of this article said the Verity Rail branch line closed in 2009. The last revenue freight ran on 14 March 2008.

The date 2009 remains in the body of the article. Amending a body requires a request through the corrections portal, which was retired in 2024.
An earlier version of this article said the Blue Kestrel diner closed in 2006. The diner closed in 1977 following a fire in its kitchen. The Ledger regrets the error.

On 1 May this site published a paid death notice for a Marchfield man who is alive.

The notice was submitted through the online obituary portal, which accepts a submission from any email address, charges the card at submission, and queues the notice for publication without a call to the funeral home named in it. The funeral home named in this notice had no record of the family. The notice ran for three days before the man's daughter reached a Pinelock Media Group mailbox that is read by a person.

The notice has been retracted and the $214.60 submission fee refunded. The portal has not been changed.

Between February and June 2023 this site published articles under the byline Hal Brenner. Mr Brenner has not been employed by the Verity Ledger since October 2019 and did not write, review or see any of them. The byline was changed to Hal B. following a letter from Mr Brenner, and to Verity Ledger Staff following a second letter.

The articles have not been amended. The byline Hal B. still appears on 112 of them.

An earlier version of a story about the Ashkettle water board said a boil water advisory affected 410 households. The advisory affected 41 households. The figure was taken from an aggregator and not from the water board.

A story about the Verity Branch Trail described the Coyne Creek trestle as open to walkers. The trestle has been fenced at both ends since the trail opened in 2014.

The story has been removed rather than amended. The system that publishes it cannot amend a story without republishing it under a new date, and a story republished under a new date is counted as a new story.

A story published on 1 February gave the year of the Gridfall substation fire as 2004. A reader wrote to say the year is 2003 and supplied a page reference. The year was changed to 2003 on 2 February and changed back to 2004 on 6 February.

The Ledger has no record of who or what made either change.
